title: Gaussian quantum reservoir computing with a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system
authors: Hajar Assil, Khadija El Anouz, Abderrahim El Allati, Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract: We propose a quantum reservoir computing framework based on a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system in the linearized Gaussian regime. The reservoir combines microwave-cavity, magnon, and mechanical degrees of freedom, and is extended by an auxiliary cavity acting as an input port, with time-dependent signals encoded in its detuning. The covariance matrix of the quadrature fluctuations provides the features for a trained linear readout. Using linear-memory, nonlinearmemory, and parity-check benchmarks, we find strong temporal memory together with more limited nonlinear processing, whose balance is controlled by the reservoir evolution time, and we show that intermode correlations substantially enhance the information accessible to the readout. The same architecture reconstructs a time-dependent signal encoded in the auxiliary-cavity detuning, with an accuracy governed by the interplay between the internal couplings and the encoding strength, and robust against Gaussian detuning noise. Accounting for finite measurement statistics reveals a trade-off between encoding strength and the precision of the covariance estimation, so that the optimal encoding depends on the available measurement budget. These results establish hybrid cavity magnomechanical systems as a promising platform for continuous-variable quantum reservoir computing with potential applications in signal probing.
summary: This paper develops a quantum reservoir computing framework utilizing a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system. By encoding time-dependent signals into the auxiliary cavity detuning, the system's covariance matrix is used to process information. The results confirm that this platform is promising for continuous-variable quantum computation, especially when leveraging inter-mode correlations.
main_problem: The paper proposes and analyzes a Gaussian quantum reservoir computing (QRC) framework to process time-dependent signals using a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system.
main_result: The system demonstrates strong temporal memory and can reconstruct time-dependent signals encoded in the input detuning, with inter-mode correlations significantly enhancing the accessible information.
method: The analysis linearizes the system dynamics around the steady state, characterizing the reservoir state via the covariance matrix, which is then used in a trained linear readout.
model_or_system: The physical system is a hybrid cavity magnomechanical setup combining microwave cavity, magnon mode, and mechanical resonator, extended with an auxiliary cavity acting as an input port.
key_observables: The covariance matrix of quadrature fluctuations, Normalized Mean-Square Error (NMSE), and the reconstructed time-dependent signal.
important_parameters: Reservoir evolution time, input modulation strength ($\epsilon\Delta$), detuning noise ($\sigma\Delta$), and the number of measurements ($N_m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis operates in the linearized Gaussian regime, and a trade-off between encoding strength and covariance estimation precision due to finite measurement statistics is noted.
figures_summary: Figures compare NMSE vs. delay ($	au$) for different encoding strengths and measurement budgets, showing the advantage of the full covariance matrix over local features.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the extended Hamiltonian and dynamics using quantum Langevin equations. It then analyzes the reservoir features using the covariance matrix, benchmarks its performance on memory tasks (linear, nonlinear, parity-check), and finally investigates the impact of noise and finite measurement statistics on signal reconstruction.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced concepts from open quantum systems (magnomechanics, cavity QED) to a computational task (QRC), providing a concrete platform for quantum information processing using controllable physical interactions.

FIG. 2. Performance of the proposed extended hybrid cav- ity magnomechanical quantum reservoir on three benchmark tasks. The NMSE is shown as a function of the delay τ for the linear-memory task, yk = sk−τ (blue circles), and the nonlinear-memory task, yk = (sk−τ)2 (orange squares). For the parity-check task (green triangles), the parity order is rep- resented as d = τ + 1 to allow the three benchmarks to be displayed on a common horizontal axis.

Fig. 2 compares the performance of the reservoir on the three benchmark tasks. A pronounced difference is observed between the linear-memory and nonlinear- processing tasks. For the linear-memory benchmark, the NMSE remains very small over a broad range of delays and increases appreciably only for the largest values of τ. This behavior indicates that information about past inputs is efficiently retained by the reservoir, demonstrat- ing a relatively long fading memory.
